title: LRU Cache
summary: Implement a cache that discards the least recently used key when inserting would exceed capacity.

contractDetails.constraints: Capacity is 1–3,000. Keys are integers in [0, 10,000] and values are integers in [0, 100,000]. There are at most 200,000 calls. The judge uses [0, key] for get and [1, key, value] for put. The output records get results only.

statement: Implement a cache that discards the least recently used key when inserting would exceed capacity. Get returns the value for a present key or −1 for a miss. A successful get or any put makes the key most recently used. Putting an existing key replaces its value. Both methods must take average constant time.

examples.explanation: Updating 8 replaces its value without occupying another slot.
Zero is a stored value. A miss returns −1.

constraints: Capacity is 1–3,000. Keys are integers in [0, 10,000] and values are integers in [0, 100,000]. There are at most 200,000 calls. The judge uses [0, key] for get and [1, key, value] for put. The output records get results only.
hints: Conceptual: Eviction depends on recency of successful use, even if a stored value has not changed.
Directional: Use a lookup table for keys and a doubly linked order from least to most recently used.
Implementation: On access, detach the entry and append it at the recent end. When over capacity, remove the oldest entry from both structures.
complexityAnalysis: O(1) average time per call and O(capacity) auxiliary space for a hash table and a recency list.
